Treat all three assertions as standard facts about initial/product topologies, proving both sides of the `Iff` independently.

- For the first conjunct, for open \(U \subseteq Y\), identify the image of \(U\) under `Subtype.coind f p hp` with
  \[
  \operatorname{Subtype.val}^{-1}(f(U)).
  \]
  Since `hf` makes \(f(U)\) open and the subtype topology is induced by `Subtype.val`, this image is open.

- For the left side of the `Iff`, use that when \(s\) is open, the subtype inclusion \(s \hookrightarrow X\) is an open map. Concretely, write an open \(t\) in the subtype as the inverse image of some open \(u \subseteq X\); its image in \(X\) is \(u \cap s\), hence open.

- For the right side, coordinate evaluation on a product,
  \[
  p \mapsto p(i),
  \]
  is continuous by the definition/universal property of the product topology, and therefore continuous at every \(x\).

Thus both propositions in the `Iff` hold unconditionally, so each implication can simply invoke the corresponding independent fact. The essential assumption in the subtype-image statement is that \(s\) is open; otherwise the subtype inclusion need not be an open map.
